**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 53, verse 1:**

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, swears by whatever of His creation He wills. Here He swears by the star (*najm*), so the *waw* is the *waw* of oath (*wāw al-qasam*), and "the star" (*al-najm*) is the thing sworn by. The word *najm* is used in the language with two meanings: the star that is in the sky, such as the sun and the moon.

Allah has said about it: ﴿And by the stars they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl: 16], meaning: in their journeys by night. And *al-najm* is also the herb that has no stalk, which camels graze in the desert.

Allah, glory be to Him, combined both meanings in His saying: ﴿The sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning, and the star and the tree prostrate﴾ [al-Rahman: 5–6].

The poet also combined them when he said:

*Arā'i al-najma fī sayrī ilayhā*
*Wa yar'āhu min al-baydā jawādiyā*

And reflect here on the precision of the Qur'anic expression: the sun and the moon point to the star of the sky, and the tree points, by association, to the star of the earth. All of them prostrate to Allah and submit to Him, the greatest thing and the least thing alike; all are equal in obedience.

In another place He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 75–76]. So the oath by the star is an oath by a great sign of Allah's signs, and the oath by the star here pertains to one of its states.

﴿By the star when it sets﴾ [al-Najm: 1], meaning: when it falls. The star is a sign in the sky that guides the traveler and shows him the way; when it falls, guidance ceases and benefit is lost. But Muhammad (ﷺ) did not go astray and did not deviate.

﴿Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred﴾ [al-Najm: 2]. This is the answer to the oath, as if He, glory be to Him, is saying: Even if the star that guides travelers falls, the star of Muhammad never falls. The star of the sky guides to material things, which are temporary, while the star of Muhammad guides to values and spiritual things, which are lasting and eternal.

The meaning of ﴿has not strayed﴾ [al-Najm: 2] is that he did not swerve from the truth or turn away from it, nor deviate from the path of guidance. ﴿Your companion﴾ [al-Najm: 2] is Muhammad (ﷺ); the companion of a people is one of them, beloved to them and held in standing among them. ﴿Nor has he erred﴾ [al-Najm: 2]: *al-ghiwāyah* (error) is false belief, and Muhammad never held a false belief at any time, even before his prophethood (*ba'tha*).

"Your companion has not strayed, nor has he gone astray."

It is as if He, glory be to Him, is saying: Even if the star that guides travelers should fall, the star of Muhammad will never fall. The star of the sky guides to material things, and these are temporary; but the star of Muhammad guides to values and to spiritual things, and these are lasting and everlasting.

The meaning of "مَا ضَلَّ" (mā ḍalla, "has not strayed"): he did not deviate from the truth, nor incline away from it, nor turn aside from the path of guidance. "صَاحِبُكُمْ" (ṣāḥibukum, "your companion"): this is Muhammad (ﷺ). The companion of a people is one of them, beloved to them and held in standing among them. "وَمَا غَوَىٰ" (wa mā ghawā, "nor has he gone astray"): ghawāya (error, going astray) is holding a false belief. Muhammad never held a false belief at any time, even before his prophethood.

This passage is a continuation of the answer to the oath: ﴿Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred﴾ [al-Najm: 2]. Here the Truth swears by another attribute of our master, the Messenger of Allah: ﴿Nor does he speak from (his own) desire﴾ [al-Najm: 3]. Al-nutq is speech, meaning that he does not speak out of his own desire, and does not bring anything from himself or by his own ijtihad (independent reasoning).

﴿It is not...﴾ [al-Najm: 4], meaning: it is not, and what is meant is the Noble Qur'an, which Muhammad recited: ﴿but it is a revelation that is revealed﴾ [al-Najm: 4], meaning from Allah. This is a construction of restriction (qasr): the Qur'an is nothing but revelation and nothing else.

﴿One mighty in power taught him﴾ [al-Najm: 5]: the one who taught it to Muhammad and revealed it to him, ﴿mighty in power﴾ [al-Najm: 5], is the trustworthy bearer of revelation, Jibril (peace be upon him). Al-quwa is the plural of quwwah (power), and he has multiple powers suited to his mission: a power of intelligence in receiving, a power of memory, and a power in transmitting and delivering. He has no desire that alters what he brings, no treachery, and no lying. These qualities are what protected the Qur'an from alteration, as earlier scriptures were altered.

Allah the Exalted has described the People of the Book: ﴿They write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," that they may sell it for a small price...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79].

The phrase ﴿mighty in power﴾ [al-Najm: 5] was explained by Him in other verses, even before the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is an honourable Qur'an, in a Book well-guarded, which none touch except the purified﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 77-79].

He also said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193], and He said: ﴿...possessor of power, with the Lord of the Throne secure, obeyed there and trustworthy﴾ [al-Takwir: 20-21]. All of these are qualities gathered in Jibril (peace be upon him).

Here He said: ﴿Possessor of strength, so he stood firm﴾ [al-Najm: 6], meaning possessor of (mirrah), which is strength in everything it undertakes, and the precision that does not err. Mirrah is a quality that strengthens a thing. You see a rope, for example, when it is twisted: its twisting is suited to its task. The rope used for hanging laundry is different from the rope with which a ship's sail is hauled.

Likewise is the mission of our master Jibril with our master Muhammad: he is to deliver this mission with strength, precision and intelligence, such that the Messenger of Allah comes with an acceptable image that is not rejected, an image in which there is enticement to receive the revelation, and which the human nature of Muhammad does not reject. Likewise the speech had sweetness, because it is the speech of Allah, not the speech of men, and it has outward signs that indicate it and its divine source.

When the revelation first came to the Messenger of Allah, it exhausted him, because it was the first time the human nature met the angelic nature. Therefore he broke out in sweat and shivered, and said: "Cover me, cover me." Thus it affected his body and soul, to the point that he feared that what had happened to him was some touch of Satan.

When he informed Lady Khadijah of the matter, and she had discernment in this matter, she said to him: "When it comes to you, tell me." So when the revelation came to him, he told her, and she sat on his knee and said: "Do you see it?" He said: "Yes." She uncovered her chest and said: "Do you see it?" He said: "No." She said: "Then it is an angel and not a devil."

Consider here the sound judgment of Lady Khadijah and her understanding before the coming of Islam. It is as if the Exalted Truth had prepared for Islam men and women who would receive its first news, support it and believe it without waiting for a miracle they could see in order to believe it, because the miracle of the Messenger of Allah for them lay in his person and his conduct among them: his miracle for them was in his truthfulness, trustworthiness, generosity and manliness.

It suffices in this context to recall the stance of al-Siddiq when they said to him: "Your companion claims that he is a prophet and that revelation comes to him." Al-Siddiq, who had been returning from a journey, said: "If he has said it, then he has spoken the truth." So the proof of his truthfulness in the view of al-Siddiq was that he says it; merely his saying it suffices for it to be true.

This meaning is evident in His saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 29], meaning: it suffices in his description that (Muhammad), whom you know, is the Messenger of Allah. The station of the Messenger of Allah among his people needs no description and no definition beyond that.

What was expected of them was that they would say: "Who is more worthy of prophethood than him?" But they said, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31].

Among the meanings of ﴿possessor of strength...﴾ [al-Najm: 6] is: possessor of good character and a good, beautiful appearance. He would come to the Messenger of Allah in the appearance he loved, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) loved to look at Dihyah al-Kalbi, so he would come in his form.

So the meaning of ﴿possessor of strength...﴾ [al-Najm: 6] is: he possesses all the good qualities that make him acceptable and not rejected, and he is described, along with that, as strong. When he appeared to the Messenger of Allah in his true form, he appeared as a beautiful bird with wings.

As the Exalted said: ﴿Possessors of wings, two, three, or four. He adds to creation what He wills...﴾ [Fatir: 1]. And it suffices to show his strength that he struck the cities of Lot with one feather of his wing, overturned them, and made their highest part their lowest.

And consider who it is that ﴿taught him, one mighty in power﴾ [al-Najm: 5]: teaching is honoured by the honour of the teacher. As we see, for example, an eloquent orator who does not commit a single grammatical error (lahn) in his sermon, and we say: "Yes, so-and-so studied under him."

Likewise, the one who taught the Messenger of Allah is Jibril, with all that he possesses of the qualities of strength, intelligence, trustworthiness and truthfulness... ﴿possessor of strength...﴾ [al-Najm: 6].

The meaning of ﴿so he stood firm﴾ [al-Najm: 6] is: Jibril taught him until the Messenger of Allah became mature and matured in the process of acquiring what suffices for guiding the world; then He entrusted him with this mission to guide people. From it is His saying about (Musa): ﴿And when he reached his maturity and became firm, We gave him judgement and knowledge; and thus do We reward the good-doers﴾ [al-Qasas: 14].

However, at the beginning, the revelation was heavy upon the Messenger of Allah, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We will impose upon you a heavy word﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 5]. So the Exalted Truth wanted to ease His Messenger from this fatigue, to give him the opportunity to taste the sweetness of what was conveyed to him and to long for it anew, so that the revelation would be lighter on his heart and his suffering would be eased.

It is known that a person customarily endures hardships in pursuit of what he loves. Therefore, when the revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah for six months, the enemies of the call seized the opportunity and said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him." Glory be to Allah! Now, in the calamity, they acknowledge the Lord of Muhammad.

Therefore Allah replied to them: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 1-5].

That is: your Lord has not bid you farewell, O Muhammad, nor has He detested you; rather He wanted you to rest.

Then He gave him an example from the reality of the movement of the universe: you, in relation to the revelation, are only like the morning and the night. The morning is for work and the night is for rest; then it returns anew so that you may turn to it with vigour and strength. Likewise, the revelation will return to you, and it will be more beloved to you and easier for you, and the Hereafter will be better for you than the first.

Moreover, the very word of farewell ﴿Your Lord has not bid you farewell, nor has He detested you﴾ [al-Duha: 3] indicates love in itself. He did not say "He has abandoned you," but "bid you farewell," and farewell is given with hope of meeting, as a beloved bids his beloved farewell upon departure.

*Al-Muntaha* (the Utmost Boundary) [An-Najm: 14] means that knowledge of creation ends there, and no one, of the angels let alone of humankind, goes beyond it. At this lote tree Jibril was seen for the second time.

However, when he was asked about seeing his Lord, glorified and exalted be He, he said: "I wonder how I could see Him." This is a precise expression from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he looked, he found only light, and light is not seen; rather, things are seen by it. So if the Real, glorified be He, is light, then there is no way to see Him, glorified be He.

Why? Because Allah has prepared us with another preparation suited to the bliss of the Hereafter.

Moreover, we eat in this world from our own cooking and preparation, whereas in the Hereafter we eat from the cooking of Allah, a cooking with precise reckoning, such that no waste remains in the body.

Likewise, among the miraculous aspects of the Night Journey and the Ascension is that Allah prepared the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a special preparation so that he could ascend. It is well known that (oxygen) is absent in the upper layers of the atmosphere.

This reality is affirmed by the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing up into the sky. The matter of seeing Allah, the Exalted, is a disputed question about which much has been said without need. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw light, and true seeing will be in the Hereafter. We must confine our speech on this matter to what has been reported concerning it, and it is a knowledge that does not benefit and an ignorance that does not harm.

What matters is the method he brought and the extent of our commitment to applying it in our practical lives. The pinnacle of this method is the prayer, which was enjoined upon him directly because of its importance in the movement of life and in straightening what is crooked in it.

We have previously given an example: a president sends an official a memo saying "do such-and-such." If the matter is more important than that, he calls him by telephone; and if it is more important still, he summons him to his office and tells him directly what he wants. This is how the prayer was.

Therefore we see it obligatory upon every Muslim, man and woman, never to be dropped under any circumstances, unlike the other acts of worship, which are dropped by valid excuses.

The hadith clarifies this station: prayer is the pillar of the religion and the support on which it stands. It also clarifies that these five prayers are not all of Islam; rather, Islam is broader in scope than them. Islam encompasses the whole movement of life, from the summit of "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah" down to removing harm from the path.

Therefore we marvel at those who call for separating the religion of Allah from the politics of this world, and who say: "There is no politics in religion and no religion in politics." This is a false saying that is not valid. Could it be permissible to leave the murderer, the adulterer, the thief and other perpetrators of crimes to act violently among the creation of Allah without punishment or deterrent?

Because of the importance of prayer in the movement of life, Allah made it a *kitaban mawquta* (a decreed writ with fixed times). Its obligation is tied to its time, and this time is distributed across the day and night, so that the believer remains in constant connection with his Lord and in constant remembrance of the method. It is not permissible to delay the prayer beyond its time except for a valid excuse accepted by the Wise Lawgiver.

Whoever sleeps through a prayer, its time is when he wakes up; and whoever forgets, its time is when he remembers. In these two cases the prayer is not made up later; rather, it is performed in the present. But if a person misses the prayer out of laziness and without excuse, it is not made up, because it has a specific time, and he has forfeited that time for himself without a legitimate excuse.

The wisdom in fixing the prayers to specific times is that a person does not know when his appointed time will overtake him, so he should hasten first to perform his prayer at its appointed time. Prayer involves continuity and persistence over the hours, unlike Hajj, for example, which is once in a lifetime.

The matter of seeing Allah, the Exalted, is a disputed question about which much has been said without need. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw light, and true seeing will be in the Hereafter. We must confine our speech on this matter to what has been reported concerning it, and it is a knowledge that does not benefit and an ignorance that does not harm.

What matters is the method he brought and the extent of our commitment to applying it in our practical lives. The pinnacle of this method is the prayer, which was enjoined upon him directly because of its importance in the movement of life and in straightening what is crooked in it.

We have previously given an example: a president sends an official a memo saying "do such-and-such." If the matter is more important than that, he calls him by telephone; and if it is more important still, he summons him to his office and tells him directly what he wants. This is how the prayer was.

Therefore we see it obligatory upon every Muslim, man and woman, never to be dropped under any circumstances, unlike the other acts of worship, which are dropped by valid excuses.

The hadith clarifies this station: prayer is the pillar of the religion and the support on which it stands. It also clarifies that these five prayers are not all of Islam; rather, Islam is broader in scope than them. Islam encompasses the whole movement of life, from the summit of "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah" down to removing harm from the path.

Therefore we marvel at those who call for separating the religion of Allah from the politics of this world, and who say: "There is no politics in religion and no religion in politics." This is a false saying that is not valid. Could it be permissible to leave the murderer, the adulterer, the thief and other perpetrators of crimes to act violently among the creation of Allah without punishment or deterrent?

Because of the importance of prayer in the movement of life, Allah made it a *kitaban mawquta* (a decreed writ with fixed times). Its obligation is tied to its time, and this time is distributed across the day and night, so that the believer remains in constant connection with his Lord and in constant remembrance of the method. It is not permissible to delay the prayer beyond its time except for a valid excuse accepted by the Wise Lawgiver.

Whoever sleeps through a prayer, its time is when he wakes up; and whoever forgets, its time is when he remembers. In these two cases the prayer is not made up later; rather, it is performed in the present. But if a person misses the prayer out of laziness and without excuse, it is not made up, because it has a specific time, and he has forfeited that time for himself without a legitimate excuse.

The wisdom in fixing the prayers to specific times is that a person does not know when his appointed time will overtake him, so he should hasten first to perform his prayer at its appointed time. Prayer involves continuity and persistence over the hours, unlike Hajj, for example, which is once in a lifetime.

What matters is that he was transferred to a higher place in responsibility: he used to be commanded while on earth, and now he is commanded while in the heavens. It is enough that Allah spoke to him without revelation through an intermediary, and it is enough that he (ﷺ) said about his seeing of his Lord, the Exalted: "..." We say: the place is for the one who sees, not for the one seen. The seer sees only in this place.

Likewise, among the miraculous aspects of the Night Journey and the Ascension is that Allah prepared the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a special preparation so that he could ascend. It is well known that (oxygen) is absent in the upper layers of the atmosphere.

This is like His saying before it: ﴿فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ مَآ أَوْحَىٰ﴾ ("Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed"), meaning: He revealed to him many great and wondrous matters, just as you say, "I honored him with what honored him."

Among these wondrous creatures around the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary there have been reported forms and colors of wondrous birds. If we see many wonders of creation in birds on earth, with their beautiful shapes that we place in cages in houses for decoration, and their voices, then what about birds that Allah placed around this Lote-Tree in the heavens?

It is also mentioned that there are golden locusts, and these golden locusts have a story with our master Dawud (peace be upon him).

As for His glorified saying: ﴿مَا زَاغَ ٱلْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَىٰ﴾ ("The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress"), meaning: the sight of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), did not swerve during this journey. "Zāgha" (زاغ) is a verb meaning to incline away from the aim. "Zāgha" conveys the meaning of "rāgha" (راغ), which occurs in the story of our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him): ﴿فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ﴾ ("So he turned to his family and brought a fat calf"), meaning: he inclined toward his family with a subtle inclination that those present did not perceive.

The difference between them is the dot on the letter zay (ز), but the meaning is one and close to it. Our saying: "Fulan zawigh" means he left secretly, in such a way that no one noticed him. Close to this meaning is also His saying, exalted is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنكُمْ لِوَاذاً﴾ ("those of you who slip away, sheltering one another") [al-Nur: 63], meaning: they slip away secretly.

As for His saying after it: ﴿وَمَا طَغَىٰ﴾ ("nor did it transgress"), meaning: his sight did not overreach, nor did it exceed the limit in seeing, nor did it extend beyond its purpose. Here we learn the etiquette of the glance and how it should be within what is permitted, like a guest who enters your house in the presence of your family and daughters, so his eye does not stretch to see what it is not lawful for him to see.

The commentary on surah 53, verse 18.

That is: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw many of the signs of Allah during the Night Journey and the Ascent (al-Isra' wa'l-Mi'raj), signs on the earth and signs in the heavens. The word ﴿ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾ [an-Najm: 18] is the feminine plural of kabira (great), while for the masculine one says kabir and akbar. The meaning is that he (ﷺ) saw many of the signs of his Lord which are described as great signs, or he saw the greatest of all the signs.

Having told us of these signs, and having sworn to the truth of our master, the Messenger of Allah, in conveying the message from his Lord, and having mentioned to us some of the cosmic signs and miracles, the discourse now turns to its counterpart: the discussion of idols and those who worship idols.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 53, verses 19-22:

The interrogative in ﴿Have you considered...﴾ [al-Najm: 19] means: tell me about these idols that you have taken as gods besides Allah. They used to take gods in various forms: a human, an animal, or a tree. Sometimes they would take an idol that had no form at all.

﴿Al-Lat﴾ [al-Najm: 19] was an idol in the shape of a man. They had a man who kneaded dough so as to relieve the women of this arduous task. When he died and left no successor to carry on this work, they grieved for him, made a statue of him to commemorate him, and then afterward they worshipped it.

﴿And al-'Uzza﴾ [al-Najm: 19] was the name of a tree they worshipped. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded Khalid to go and cut it down, and he (ﷺ) used to say:

O 'Uzza, your denial, not your forgiveness!
Indeed, I have seen that Allah has humiliated you.

﴿And Manat, the third, the other﴾ [al-Najm: 20]. Manat was also the name of an idol of theirs. He said ﴿the third, the other﴾ [al-Najm: 20], meaning that it was their third (deity), and it was not in the form of a human or an animal. He said ﴿the other﴾ [al-Najm: 20] as a way of belittling them and mocking them and those who worshipped them.

Allah, glorified and exalted, made them judges over what they do and over their worship of idols. He said to them: tell me about these idols. Do they deserve to be worshipped? Do they have power or will, when they are stones that you brought with your own hands and shaped into a form you desired?

Then, when the idol falls and the wind knocks it over, you set it up again, and when its arm breaks, you repair it. So how do you worship them? Where are your minds?

But this is the nature of religiosity in the human fitrah (innate disposition). The Creator, glorified be He, has created man with a disposition toward religion, and before Adam was created, while he was still in the realm of dhar (the primordial realm of souls), He took the covenant from us, while we were in the realm of dhar in the loins of Adam, peace be upon him.

So He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this," or say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172-173].

So: they worshipped idols because of the faith of the fitrah that is in the soul. But faith carries obligations and requirements that may be hard on the soul and restrict its movement toward desires. So man inclines toward worshipping a god without obligation, in order to satisfy the instinct of religiosity in his soul. For this reason they worshipped idols, because in their assumption they were gods, but they have no requirements and no methodology. They only worshipped them for the comfort of their emotional faith experiences.

Here we notice the precision of the Qur'anic expression in His saying: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [al-Najm: 19-20]. They also worshipped the angels besides Allah, but He did not mention them along with al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, because the angels are not seen.

It would not be correct to say: "Have you considered the angels?" because they had not seen the angels. They had only heard about them and believed in them unseen. They said regarding all of these: "They are our intercessors with Allah." And they said: ﴿We only worship them so that they bring us closer to Allah in position﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. So, even in their disbelief in Allah, they resort to Allah as a pretext.

His saying: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female?﴾ [al-Najm: 21] is an interrogative for amazement and rebuke against them, since they attributed the angels to Allah, the Exalted, and made them females because of the presence of the feminine ta' marbuta in the word.

The angels are created beings of Allah, the Exalted, made of light. They do not eat, drink, or reproduce, and they are not described as male or female.

So this is an unjust judgment and a division that the Qur'an called ﴿an unfair division﴾ [al-Najm: 22], unjust and oppressive, because you attributed to yourselves the superior kind and to Allah the inferior kind. The first error was that they made the angels female, and the second that they worshipped them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 53, verse 23:

The discussion remains connected to the idols: al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat. The Exalted Lord speaks about them, saying ﴿They are nothing but names﴾. That is, these idols are nothing but names ﴿which you and your fathers have named, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾. They are names of your own invention, given to idols made by your own hands.

It is well known that a name is given to indicate a named thing. These idols, however, are names without a named reality, so they are false. You called them gods, while they are stones that neither harm nor benefit.

﴿Which you and your fathers have named﴾: this is because they inherited them from the forefathers and grandfathers, as He relates of them: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾. Thus they acknowledged the error of their fathers, and that they were proceeding upon their method.

Then He clarifies to them the falsehood of their beliefs: ﴿for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾. That is, these are from yourselves and not from Allah; there is no proof or evidence for their truth, and you and your fathers are not legislators.

Legislation and matters of creed are not taken from humans; they are taken from Allah. These people do not follow the guidance of Allah. Rather, ﴿they follow only conjecture﴾: here "in" (إِن) is a negation meaning "they do not follow except conjecture". ﴿And what the souls desire﴾: they do not follow realities or facts.

Conjecture (ẓann) is one of the six verbal relations (al-nisab al-kalamiyya) that we previously explained, namely: knowledge ('ilm), ignorance (jahl), imitation (taqlid), doubt (shakk), conjecture (ẓann) and illusion (wahm). A verbal relation that has a certain reality and for which evidence can be established is knowledge; and if it has a certain reality but there is no evidence for it, it is imitation.

If the verbal relation has no reality, it is ignorance. This applies to a relation held with certainty. If the verbal relation is not held with certainty, meaning that it may happen or may not happen, then if the two sides are equal, this is doubt; if the occurrence is more probable, it is conjecture; and if the occurrence is less probable, it is illusion.

Conjecture may be acted upon in ordinary matters. For example, if we wished to travel to Alexandria and I said to my companion, "This road is easy and has the requirements of travel," and he said, "I think the other road is better because it is newer and such-and-such," then it is permissible for me to leave the certainty I know about the road and take the other road that is conjectured, because if the choice turns out to be wrong, the harm resulting from it is small.

As for matters of religion and creed, certainty must be followed, not conjecture. The Exalted Lord informs us that these people followed conjecture in matters of worship. They said: God, may He be exalted, has majesty and greatness, and we cannot approach Him and worship Him directly, but we worship something else that brings us near to Him and intercedes for us with Him.

Therefore, His saying ﴿they follow only conjecture﴾ means: in belief, ﴿and what the souls desire﴾ means: in conduct and action, they follow the desire of the soul. The word "hawa" (desire) is applied to what is blameworthy among the things the soul seeks.

﴿And there has certainly come to them from their Lord the guidance﴾: the lam is for emphasis, and "qad" is a particle of confirmation.

He, glory be to Him, wishes to emphasize this reality: that the guidance of Allah has come to them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conveyed to them the method of Allah. Yet they abandoned the truth and certainty, and followed conjecture and what the souls desire. Had they followed conjecture and desire before the method of truth came to them, they would have had an excuse. But since they did this after the guidance from Allah had come to them, they have no excuse and no proof.

Do they think, having turned away from the guidance of God toward false conjectures, that a person walks through this world according to his own whims? And that he will have whatever he wishes, even if his wishes oppose the method of his Lord? The reality is that he does not have that, because religion and belief are not taken by wishful thinking, and the Truth, glory be to Him, is not according to your desire.

Tamanni (wishing) means seeking something that cannot be reached and whose occurrence is not possible. Wishing means nothing more than that you love the thing you wish for. Yes, you love it, but it will not happen...

They wish for this, wishing that a person may have whatever he wants and loves without restraints. This is a wish, and a wish is something a person loves, but it does not come true, because a person does not control the circumstances relating to it, and does not possess the causes that would fulfill everything he desires. Rather, he has a Lord who decrees destinies, actions, good and evil.

In several verses, the Truth, glory be to Him, explains the wishes of these people. Among their wishes is their saying: ﴿We only worship them so that they bring us closer to God in nearness﴾ (al-Zumar 39:3). Among their wishes is what the Qur'an relates about the owner of the garden in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination﴾ (al-Kahf 18:36).

In another place, one of them said: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have with Him the best﴾ (Fussilat 41:50). Thus, a person's wishing for himself does not stop at any limit. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless﴾ (Fussilat 41:49).

Among their wishes is what the Qur'an relates about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"? Has he attained knowledge of the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ (Maryam 19:77-78). Neither of these is the case, for he has not attained knowledge of the unseen, and he has no covenant with God that He will give him what he wants.

Then God responds to him: ﴿No! We will record what he says and extend for him of the punishment an extension. And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone﴾ (Maryam 19:79-80).

So: a person does not have whatever he wishes. How could he, when the matter entirely belongs to God alone, in the first life and in the Hereafter? ﴿To God belongs the Hereafter and the first life﴾ (al-Najm 53:25). Here is a restrictive construction (uslub qasr) by placing the predicate, the prepositional phrase, before the subject, meaning: to God alone belongs the Hereafter and the first life.

He placed the Hereafter first because they had said about the idols: "These are our intercessors with God," so He informed them that the Hereafter belongs to God alone, and this intercession will not benefit you because it is false. ﴿And the first life﴾ (al-Najm 53:25) means: what they wish for in this world, which they have no power to achieve.

Some have said: He placed the Hereafter before the first life although the natural order is "the first life and the Hereafter," because the Hereafter is the point of dispute between one who affirms it and one who denies it, and the point of doubt regarding its occurrence. Therefore He placed it first to emphasize that it is a truth, and a truth more emphatic than the first life, which you have witnessed.

The reality is that he is not granted that, because religion and creed are not obtained through wishful thinking, and the Truth, glory be to Him, does not follow your desires.

Oh, would that youth could return one day, so I could tell it what old age has done.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 53, verse 26:

When they believed that the idols would intercede for them with God, and said: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to God in closeness﴾ [al-Zumar: 3], God refuted them with what makes clear the falsehood of their belief. How, then, do you expect the intercession of idols with God, when the angels brought near and the honoured servants with Him have no intercession except by His permission, glory be to Him?

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how many an angel in the heavens, whose intercession avails nothing except after God gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾. That is, many of the angels. Here kam (how many) is khabariyyah (a descriptive "how many"), which indicates abundance, since it asks about a number that has no limit.

So there are two conditions for the acceptance of the intercession of the angels. The first condition: that God permits the angel to intercede. The second: that He is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made. God is not pleased except with the people of pure monotheism. This is an honour for the intercessor and an honour for the one for whom intercession is made.

God, may He be exalted, says in the Verse of the Throne: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

If this is the state of the angels in accepting intercession, though they are honoured servants who do not speak before Him, and by His command they act, and He said of them: ﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6], then how much more so is the intercession of idols (impossible)?

We observe in the Qur'anic expression in this verse that the word malak (angel) came in the singular form, and then He reported about the singular with the plural form, saying: ﴿their intercession avails nothing﴾, and did not say "his intercession."

They said: because kam khabariyyah indicates abundance, when it combined with the singular it gave it the meaning of the plural. So the meaning is "how many an angel," that is, many angels, and what would be appropriate is to say "their intercession," in the plural form.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 53, verse 27:

God, exalted is He, exposes their false belief in their saying: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us closer to God in nearness﴾ [Az-Zumar: 3], and in their regarding the angels as intercessors for them with God. This is mere talk and feeble arguments, because at root they do not believe in the Hereafter, so how can they speak of intercession?

﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ [An-Najm: 27], that is, the disbelievers, ﴿surely name the angels with the name of females﴾ [An-Najm: 27], that is, they claim that the angels are daughters of God. ﴿And they have no knowledge of it﴾ [An-Najm: 28], meaning they have no knowledge for this saying ﴿of it﴾ [An-Najm: 28].

In another place He, exalted is He, said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misleading ones as helpers﴾ [Al-Kahf: 51].

So: they have no knowledge of the creation of the angels. In this claim they are liars, saying what they do not know. The matter is that in this question they follow their false conjecture; they supposed the angels to be females because of the feminine marker (ta' al-ta'nith, the feminine ending) in the word for angels (malā'ika).

﴿And conjecture does not avail against the truth in anything﴾ [An-Najm: 28], that is, this conjecture of theirs is false, having no real connection to reality and no benefit against it. The truth in this matter is what God has told us, since He is their Creator and knows them best, and conjecture can never take the place of certain, clear knowledge.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 53, verse 28:

﴿And they have no knowledge of it.﴾ That is: they have no knowledge of this claim.

In another place He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misguiders as helpers.﴾ [al-Kahf: 51].

So: there is no knowledge with them concerning the creation of the angels. In this claim they are liars, saying what they do not know. The matter is that in this question they follow their false conjecture (zann). They supposed the angels to be females because of the presence of the feminine marker (ta' al-ta'nith) in the word malā'ika (angels).

﴿And conjecture does not avail against the truth at all.﴾ That is: their conjecture is false; it has no connection to reality and does not suffice in its place. The truth in this matter is what God has told us, for He is their Creator and the most knowing of them. Conjecture can never take the place of certain, clear knowledge.

Following the explanation of how Allah the Exalted described the stance of the Prophet's opponents, showing that they do not seek the truth but pursue their desires, suspicions and appetites, He says to him: "O Muhammad, relieve yourself of these people, for there is no benefit in them."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was extremely eager for the guidance of his people, and in his effort to call them to the truth he burdened himself beyond what he could bear. Therefore Allah addressed him, saying: ﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this discourse.﴾ [al-Kahf: 6] and said to him: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance [of the message]...﴾ [al-Shura: 48].

We have explained that Allah does not want from them forms that come compelled; rather He wants hearts that come to Him willingly and by choice.

Therefore He says to His Prophet: ﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our remembrance...﴾ [al-Najm: 29]. "Fa-a'ridh" (so turn away) is the imperative of the verb 'arada (to show, to present) — "a'rada 'arid" (he showed, presented, so he is a presenter), and "mu'ridh" (one who turns away). The hamza here is called hamzat al-izalah (the hamza of removal), meaning the removal of the presentation. You know the international exhibition (al-ma'radh al-dawli) where products are displayed, for the owner of the product presents it to people and explains its merits, so he is a presenter ('arid).

Likewise the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to present guidance and the method of truth to his people, explaining to them its aims and merits, but they responded only with patience-testing, harm, turning away from him, and withdrawal.

He continued like this until his Lord commanded him to turn away from them, so He said to him: ﴿Fa-a'ridh﴾ [al-Najm: 29] — from a'rada, which is the opposite of 'arada. The hamza of removal transforms the verb into its opposite: just as they turned away from you, turn away from them; they turned away from you, so you turn away from them.

The hamza of removal in a'rada is like that in a'jama. We say: a'jama al-kitab, meaning he removed its ambiguity (ujmah); from it comes mu'jam, the book that removes the obscurity of words. Similarly, a'rada means he removed the presentation.

﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our remembrance﴾ [al-Najm: 29]. Thus, they are the ones who initiated turning away from the remembrance of Allah, that is, from the Qur'an and from the method, because it restricts their freedom in their appetites. The method is an obligation, and they do not want obligation; they want to run freely after their desires and pleasures without a watchman.

If these turners-away from Allah were to reflect, they would know that it is in their own interest. For example, when He forbids you from theft, and you are an individual, He is forbidding all people from stealing from you, restraining your hand and the hands of millions from you.

So, before you look at the hardship of obligations, look at their benefits...

As for His saying, ﴿and he desires nothing but the life of this world﴾ [al-Najm: 29], meaning this is their goal, so they work for nothing but it, and they have acknowledged this when they said: ﴿It is not but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24]. So the Hereafter is not in their calculations.

Therefore Allah the Exalted disparages this view and says: ﴿That is their extent of knowledge...﴾ [al-Najm: 30].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 53, verse 30:

﴿That is the extent of their knowledge.﴾

The utmost that they reached of self-acquired knowledge, this is where it brought them to a halt.

What is remarkable is that they closed their ears and stopped their hearing against guidance, so they did not take up the knowledge of God that He sent down to them. ﴿Indeed your Lord knows best who strays from His way, and He knows best who is guided.﴾

We pause first at the style of restriction (qasr) in ﴿He knows best﴾ (huwa a'lam), where knowledge is restricted to God alone. This is because guidance and misguidance are, for the most part, unseen matters that none can perceive except the Knower of the secret and what is yet more hidden. Moreover, everyone claims to be upon guidance and claims that others are upon error, so God has reserved this knowledge for Himself, glorified be He.

This verse came after the saying of the Exalted to His Prophet: ﴿So turn away from one who turns his back on Our Reminder﴾ [al-Najm: 29]. Here there is a correspondence between the two verses, because God, exalted be He, had already foreknown His creation: who will go astray and who will be guided, who will heed the call and who will turn away from it.

Therefore He said to His Prophet: ﴿Ease your soul; upon you is only the conveying [of the message]﴾ [al-Shura: 48]. The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, informed His Messenger of who would be guided and who would remain upon his misguidance. Abu Lahab, Abu Sufyan, 'Amr and Khalid ibn al-Walid were all in one trench against Islam, yet God willed that Abu Sufyan, Khalid and 'Amr would believe.

As for Abu Lahab, he remained upon his disbelief, even after the revelation about him: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! * His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. * He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame﴾ [al-Masad: 1-3].

This is also a restrictive construction through the fronting of the predicate: i.e., to Allah alone.

In another verse He, exalted is He, says: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Shura: 49]. The heavens and the earth are wondrous in themselves, and what is within them is more wondrous: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Najm: 31]. And He said: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Nahl: 77].

These are three stages of Allah's dominion. He, glorified is He, possesses the container, the heavens and the earth; He possesses the contained, that is, what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, each of which is wondrous; and He possesses what is more wondrous than that, namely what is hidden from us in the kingdom (malakut) of the heavens and the earth.

This means that you, O human being, should not disdain deduction (istinbat), for the cosmos is full of what you know and what you do not know of signs and wonders, and in it are bounties that do not end and do not run out, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure. When the wonders and secrets are exhausted with the passing of this world, the wonders and secrets of the Hereafter will come.

Then He, exalted is He, makes clear that this dominion over the heavens and the earth entails recompense in the Hereafter, because the dominion is Allah's dominion, the creation is Allah's creation, the messengers are Allah's messengers, and the method is Allah's method. So before you, O human being, lies the vast cosmos and what is in it of cosmic signs that point to the power of the Creator, glorified is He. So infer the Creator from creation.

Then He sent you messengers, revealed the books, legislated the laws, explained the lawful and the unlawful, explained the prescribed limits, and explained the recompense. So the dominion of the heavens and the earth must end in recompense, and recompense must necessarily be of the same kind as the deed: ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [al-Najm: 31].

The signs are three, as we have said: cosmic signs that point to the power of Allah; miraculous signs that point to the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from Allah; and the rulings (ayat al-ahkam) that the noble Qur'an contains. Whoever does not take heed from these signs and does not receive them well has done evil, and will be recompensed for his evil.

Whoever receives them well is recompensed for his good, as if he has greeted the Responsible One, glorified and exalted is He, with obedience, and so Allah greets him with something better than it: ﴿and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [al-Najm: 31], that is, with what is better than what they offered. If we have been commanded in this world to return a greeting with something better, then Allah is more entitled to that.

Reflect here on the appropriateness of the expression and the precision of the delivery. He did not say, "that He may recompense those who did evil with evil," but ﴿according to what they did﴾ [al-Najm: 31]. He did not confront them with the word "evil," but set before them the deed they had done.

In this is an indication of Allah's justice: ﴿And Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 117]. Then He places the recompense of the people of evil before the recompense of the people of good, so that recompense with the best is the last thing to strike our hearing.

Then the verses explain and elaborate on those who did good, and the aspects of good in their deeds.

Among the characteristics of those who did good is that they avoid the major sins (kaba'ir al-ithm) and the abominations (al-fawahish). That is, they completely abandon major sins and do not approach this forbidden domain, except for (illa al-lamam), which refers to minor sins (saghair al-dhunub).

Thus God, in His mercy toward His creatures, has undertaken to erase minor sins for us, and He has made for them an eraser that removes them: the five daily prayers, on the condition that we avoid major sins.

In the hadith: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiation for what lies between them, provided major sins are avoided." Whoever does this and follows this path will have the best reward (al-husna), and will be among the people of ihsan (excellence).

So: the ithm and the fawahish are the great sins for which God has threatened those who commit them, and the fawahish are the sins that are grave and monstrous among the major sins. God has prescribed for them a punishment and a fixed penalty (hadd).

As for the lamam that God excepted and pardoned, it is the lamam, meaning: minor, trivial sins from which no great harm follows. This too is conditional on not being bold in them or persisting in them until they become a habit for you.

And if God Most High deals with you in this manner, then be modest before Him, glorified is He, and do not be bold toward Him even with minor sins, for a small sin, when added to another small sin, and when there is persistence and insistence in the matter, becomes a great sin. Then it behooves the sensible person to consider against whose right this sin is committed: it is against the right of God. So, then: refrain.

They said: these verses were revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. The beginning of his connection with the call to truth was that he turned away from it and refused to listen to the Qur'an. Then his heart softened and he was impressed by what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was saying, so he gave a little of his security to the matter of the call and became content with it.

Then he recalled his honour and standing among his people, and feared that it would be said he had abandoned the religion of the fathers and forefathers, so he turned back on his heels and retreated. They also said: a man came to him and warned him against believing in Muhammad, and said to him: "If you are afraid of the punishment, I will bear it for you in exchange for your giving me such-and-such," so he gave him, then he retracted and withheld it.

They also said: it was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith as well: a man came to him and said: "The punishment of God is severe, and I will bear it for you; give me five qalas (she-camels), that is, five camels," but he considered them too many, so he withheld this gift from the man. They also said: it was revealed concerning Safwan.

The meaning of ﴿Have you seen him who turns away﴾ [al-Najm: 33] O Muhammad, i.e., turned away from you, left you and went on; ﴿and gives a little, then withholds﴾ [al-Najm: 34] i.e., from giving, or from security.

﴿And withholds﴾ [al-Najm: 34] means he withheld his gift. It is from al-kadya (hard ground). They say: "So-and-so dug the pit and it went straight for him," meaning he found what he was hoping for in it; and "So-and-so dug the pit and it became hard (akda'at)," meaning he found nothing, or he found a large rock that prevented him from reaching his aim, and this rock is called a kadya. From it our saying "a steep obstacle" ('aqaba ka'da'), meaning: something that prevents you from reaching your goal.

﴿Has he knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾ [al-Najm: 35] Has he gained knowledge of the unseen and known the reality that this man will indeed fulfil his undertaking to bear the punishment for him? ﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled [his covenant]?﴾ [al-Najm: 36-37] meaning: Did this one who turns away from the call to truth not learn what came in the scriptures of Moses and in the scriptures of Abraham?

﴿That no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another...﴾.

Likewise, in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾ [An-Najm: 44], the attached pronoun is emphasised by a separate pronoun, because the matter of giving life and causing death carries the suspicion of partnership. Some may think that the physician, for example, is the one who caused the patient to die or gave him life, or that the killer is the one who caused the slain to die.

So the Truth, glorified is He, reserves these matters for Himself alone, to the exclusion of all others: ﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾ [An-Najm: 44]. The reality is that when the slain man was killed, the killer did not cause his death; rather, his appointed term coincided with that blow and so he died. He died because he was going to die at that moment, even if the killer had not struck him.

Therefore He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿He who created death and life..﴾ [Al-Mulk: 2]. Death and life are the creation of God alone, with no part for anyone in them. Hence the poet said:

Whoever does not die by the sword dies by other means; the causes are many, but death is one.

And they said: death without apparent causes is itself the cause. That is, he died because he was going to die.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female﴾ [An-Najm: 45]. Note here that He, glorified is He, did not say "and that He, it is He," because the matter does not need this emphasis. The creation is something everyone grants to God; no one has claimed it for himself, and there is no suspicion of partnership in creation.

The meaning of "the pairs" (al-zawjayn) is the two kinds, male and female. A zawj is a single individual with its counterpart, as in His saying: ﴿eight pairs, two of the sheep..﴾ [Al-An'am: 143].

﴿from a drop when it is emitted﴾ [An-Najm: 46]. The origin of creation is a nutfah, which is a drop of semen.

﴿when it is emitted﴾ [An-Najm: 46]. That is, it is propelled and discharged into the womb of the woman, and from it the child comes into being by God's power.

This verse has resolved for us a problem over which scholars long disputed: some believed that the woman is responsible for whether the child is male or female. But when we read here ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female * from a drop when it is emitted﴾ [An-Najm: 45–46], we know with certainty that the man is responsible for this matter. The nutfah is the man's nutfah, which he deposits in the womb of his wife; the wife, then, is the receiver, giving back what she has received.

We have also said that the Arab woman, by her nature and innate disposition, arrived at this truth. A woman whose husband took another wife over her because she bore him only daughters said:

"What is it with Abu Hamza that he does not come to us, but stays in the house beside ours,
angry that we do not bear him sons? By God, that is not in our hands;
we are like the earth for those who plant in it; we give them what we were given."

Thus the Arab woman, by her disposition, reached what scholars reached later. We must distinguish between the nutfah and the maniyy: the nutfah is the fluid in which the spermatozoon lives, while the maniyy is the very microbe from which the child comes.

May God have mercy on al-Aqqad when he said: half a sewing thimble contains the offspring of the whole world, and one ejaculation of a man can fill half a thimble. Glory be to God.

It means: do not think that this world is the final destination. He who brought you into being in this worldly existence is able to bring you back in another creation on the Day of Resurrection, as He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation? Nay, but they are in confusion about a new creation﴾ [Qaf: 15].

The new creation will be in the Hereafter, when Allah raises the dead. He who created from nothing at the beginning is all the more able to restore them from the remains of the first creation. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Book﴾ [Qaf: 4].

﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾ [al-Najm: 48]. Note here the restriction and emphasis through repeating the independent pronoun after the attached pronoun. This shows us that the matter of provision, wealth and poverty belongs to Allah alone, and no one has any share in it. He alone, glorified is He, drives the provisions and makes this one rich and that one poor.

So, when the suspicion arose that someone shares with Allah in this matter, the verse came in this style. If we took power for homes directly from the high-voltage line at the substations, the devices and lamps in the house would burn, because the weak cannot receive directly from the strong; rather a regulator or (transformer) is necessary. Thus the sun is in relation to Sirius.

Known that ʿĀd is the people of Prophet Hūd (peace be upon him), whom Allah destroyed with a violent, furious wind when they denied their prophet. As for the words ﴿ʿĀdan al-Ūlā﴾ [An-Najm: 50], the meaning is that there was another ʿĀd. They said: when the wind descended upon them, it destroyed those of them who were present in this place where the punishment descended, and there were scattered groups among them who gathered together, sought a safe place, and went to Makkah; and this is the other ʿĀd.

﴿And Thamūd, so He left none﴾ [An-Najm: 51]. Just as He destroyed ʿĀd, He destroyed Thamūd with the Blast, ﴿so He left none﴾ [An-Najm: 51], He spared none of them.

Likewise, ﴿and the people of Nūḥ before, indeed they were more wrongful and more tyrannical﴾ [An-Najm: 52]. Allah destroyed them, then He distinguished them from their predecessors by two qualities: ﴿indeed they were themselves more wrongful and more tyrannical﴾ [An-Najm: 52].

So: wrongdoing and tyranny existed among ʿĀd and among Thamūd, but the people of Nūḥ were (ʾaẓlam), more intense in wrongdoing, and (ʾaṭghā), more intense in tyranny. Sufficient as evidence of this is that their prophet remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and only a few believed with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 53, verses 53–54:

﴿And the overturned cities (al-Mu'tafikah)﴾ [al-Najm: 53] are coordinated with ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of Nūḥ. They are the cities of the people of Lūṭ (Lot), and they were called al-Mu'tafikah because Allah, exalted is He, overturned them upside down and made their upper part their lower part. For this reason we call falsehood ifk (ifk, "a perversion"), because it turns realities upside down, and from this comes the incident of the slander (ḥādithat al-ifk) that touched Sayyidah ʿĀ'ishah in Surat al-Nūr.

The meaning of ﴿ahwā﴾ [al-Najm: 53] is that they fell and collapsed, because the angels lifted them up to the expanse of the sky and then overturned them upon those who were in them. ﴿So there covered them that which covered﴾ [al-Najm: 54]: "covered them" means that what descended upon them overwhelmed and enveloped them, or concealed them.

﴿Mā ghashshā﴾ [al-Najm: 54]: the mā here is exclamatory (ta'ajjubiyyah), indicating an abundance that surpasses description. That is: there covered them a terrible, wondrous matter and a fearsome dread, yes, because Allah, exalted is He, gathered upon the people of Lūṭ various kinds of punishment at one time or in succession, one after another.

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when Our command came﴾ [Hūd: 82], meaning: for their destruction, ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of hard clay, layered, * marked from your Lord. And it is not from the wrongdoers far away﴾ [Hūd: 82-83].

The meaning of ﴿musawwamah﴾ [Hūd: 83] is "marked," i.e., each stone bore the name of its target, so they were not random; rather they were calculated with precision. The stone descends upon its owner and does not exceed him. Similar to them are the stones with which the companions of the Elephant were struck: ﴿And He sent against them birds in flocks * striking them with stones of hard clay﴾ [al-Fīl: 3-4].

It is strange, after the Qur'anic context has explicitly stated the word "stones," that we hear someone say: rather, it was a microbe or a virus that struck them all. A microbe has an incubation period before it becomes active, whereas this punishment descended upon them in that very moment.

Almighty Allah consoles His Messenger (ﷺ) and reassures him of Allah's support for him and His confirmation of the call. The way of Allah with calls to truth is that the matter ends with the victory of truth, and here are the signs that remain as witnesses to the destruction of those who denied. So He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, * And by night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [as-Saffat: 137-138]. Their traces remain, which you see night and day.

The Exalted says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you dispute?﴾ [an-Najm: 55]. Which blessings of your Lord, O Muhammad, ﴿will you dispute?﴾ [an-Najm: 55]. Al-mira' means doubt or argument. It is as if He, the Exalted, is saying to him: be reassured, for Allah will complete His blessings upon you.

In Surat ar-Rahman: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?﴾ [ar-Rahman: 13]. The address is to mankind and the jinn. When the Messenger (ﷺ) recited it, he said: "[Rather], it is legitimate for us to respond to the Qur'an when we hear it with what fits the situation: when praise is mentioned we praise Allah, when glorification is mentioned we say 'Subhan Allah' (Glory be to Allah), when Paradise is mentioned we ask Allah for it, when the Fire is mentioned we seek refuge in Allah from it, and so on."

There is a difference between silent admiration suppressed within the soul and admiration that is spoken and expressed. Moreover, when you express your interaction with the Qur'an verbally, you become an example in that for those who hear you.

The word (ayy) here indicates abundance, and (ala'') means blessings, plural of (ala) meaning a single blessing. Al-mira' means argument, which takes place between two parties, each striving to establish his proof against the other. In the lexicon, al-mira' is taken in two senses: the twisting of a rope (maru al-habl), meaning twisting it to strengthen it, and the number of strands twisted depends on the purpose of the rope. Or it is taken from (yamri al-naqa), meaning milking the she-camel and drawing out everything in her udder.

So: you argue to strengthen your proof, or you argue to bring out everything in the opponent's quiver.

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿This...﴾ [al-Najm: 56] refers to the Prophet (ﷺ) and the true message he brought. The warner is the one who warns people and cautions them against evil before its time. ﴿Of the former warnings﴾ [al-Najm: 56], meaning the warnings that came before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) through the processions of earlier messengers. The greatness of warning in our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), is that he is the last warner and the Seal of the Messengers, all of them.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Imminent has drawn near﴾ [al-Najm: 57], meaning the Hour has drawn near, as though he (ﷺ) came at the very mouth of the Hour. After he said ﴿This is a warner﴾ [al-Najm: 56], he followed it with ﴿The Imminent has drawn near﴾ [al-Najm: 57].

For this reason, the noble hadith (a saying of the Prophet (ﷺ)) states: his (ﷺ) being sent is counted among the signs of the Hour.

His Lord, Exalted is He, also addressed him saying: ﴿About what are you in mention of it?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 43], meaning: about the remembrance of the Hour and its signs. Since the Imminent has drawn near, be alert. This is the last of the messages, so cling to it and hold fast to this Seal of the Messengers and final warner, after whom there is no warner, and you will be saved by him.

From the meaning of ﴿has drawn near﴾ [al-Najm: 57] we understand that it is the one that seeks you and pursues you with swift steps that hasten toward you. Shortly after, at the beginning of al-Qamar, He will say: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1].

﴿Besides God, none can remove it﴾ [al-Najm: 58], meaning: when the terrors of the Hour arrive, no one other than God can repel them. In the affairs of this world and the trials of life, there may be someone who relieves your distress or repels evil from you.

As for the Hereafter, the matter is momentous, and no one has the power to repel it. Otherwise, how could one repel it when it is the Great Catastrophe that encompasses everyone? How could he repel it from you when he cannot repel it from himself?

So then: prepare yourselves for this situation, and take for yourselves a protector from God, for He alone, without partner, is able to repel from you on this Day.

There is nothing strange in the Imminent having drawn near and the Hour having approached, for its minor signs have already appeared in the reality of life, as our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), informed us, and his saying: , and his saying: . And other signs besides these that we have actually witnessed. So why be amazed?

Surah 53, verses 59–62, in the commentary of al-Sha'rawi:

The hamza here is an interrogative of wonder. They marvel at ﴿this discourse﴾ [al-Najm: 59], that is, at the Qur'an, while He marvels at them. He says to them: Do you marvel at the Qur'an? It is more fitting for you to marvel at your own state and at what you are engaged in of heedless play and turning away from the truth, and this makes you miss the opportunity and deprives you of much good.

The same meaning applies to ﴿and you laugh and do not weep﴾ [al-Najm: 60]: you laugh in mockery and derision, and it was more fitting for you to weep over yourselves and over the good that has escaped you. ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾ [al-Najm: 61], meaning heedless and negligent.

This is the state of those whose hearts have hardened and whom Satan and the self have overcome. You see them, alongside their turning away from the truth, mocking its people and laughing at them in derision.

As Allah the Exalted said in depicting this scene: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29] — He called them criminals — ﴿used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they winked at one another. And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as guardians over them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29–33].

Yes, this is the state of the people of falsehood who reverse the realities in this world. But this world is not the goal, nor is it the final destination, for there is the Last Day on which the oppressor and the oppressed are separated, as they said: "And before Allah the adversaries are gathered."

So Allah reassures the people of faith: ﴿So today﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34] — that is, the Day of Reckoning — ﴿those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34], and whoever laughs last laughs longest. ﴿Upon couches, they will look. Has the disbelievers' reward been paid for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 35–36]. And then we say: Yes, O Lord, You have requited them according to what they deserved.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿so prostrate to Allah and worship﴾ [al-Najm: 62], we note first the concise style of Qur'anic expression, which leaves room for the discernment of the hearer. The meaning is: prostrate to Allah and worship Allah, for He alone deserves worship, with no partner. The command to worship is directed only to Him, glorified is He, even if the object of worship is not mentioned.

When the Real, glorified and exalted is He, commands them to prostrate, submit and obey, it is as if He says to them: It would have been more fitting for you to weep, submit and humble yourselves, and to hold fast to this truth that has come to you to take you by the hand. It is the rope of salvation, so do not meet it with mockery.
